title: Residential Property Disclosure Statement
description: Virginia Code §55.1-700 et seq. requires sellers of residential real property (containing 1-4 dwelling units) to furnish a Residential Property Disclosure Statement to the buyer. Virginia's disclosure is a notice-based system — the owner disclaims representations and puts the buyer on notice to conduct independent inspections. The form states the property is being sold 'as-is' but the owner must still make specific disclosures about known defects, pending assessments, and adverse conditions.

required_actions.note: Must be provided before ratification of contract. Buyer has right to void if not received. Notice-based system rather than condition-based.

metadata.note: Virginia uses a notice-based disclosure system, not a condition report. Sellers disclaim warranties.

title: Agency Disclosure and Brokerage Relationships
description: Virginia requires licensees to disclose their brokerage relationship in writing at the earliest practical time. Virginia recognizes standard agent, limited service agent, independent contractor (no agency), and dual/designated representation. Dual representation requires written informed consent from both parties under Va. Code §54.1-2138.

required_actions.note: Must be provided at first substantive discussion about a specific property.

title: Closing Practice — Attorney or Settlement Agent
description: Virginia does not strictly require attorney involvement at closing, but settlement agents must be licensed under the Virginia Consumer Real Estate Settlement Protection Act (CRESPA). Licensed attorneys, title insurance companies, and approved settlement agents may conduct closings. Virginia uses deed of trust rather than traditional mortgage instruments.

required_actions.note: Settlement agent must be CRESPA-licensed. Attorney involvement recommended but not required.

title: Military Air Installation Noise Zone Disclosure
description: Virginia Code §55.1-708 requires disclosure if a property is located in a noise zone or accident potential zone designated by the Virginia Department of Defense Affairs near a military air installation. This is unique to Virginia given the significant military presence in the state.

required_actions.note: Must disclose if property is in noise zone or accident potential zone near military air installation.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Federal law requires disclosure of known lead-based paint hazards for residential properties built before 1978. Virginia follows federal requirements. Sellers must provide the EPA pamphlet and allow a 10-day inspection contingency.

title: HOA/Condo Resale Disclosure Package
description: Virginia requires sellers of properties in homeowners associations or condominiums to provide a resale disclosure packet under the Virginia Property Owners Association Act (§55.1-1800 et seq.) or the Virginia Condominium Act (§55.1-1900 et seq.). The packet must include financials, rules, pending litigation, and reserve study information. Buyer has 3 days to void after receipt.

required_actions.note: Association must deliver within 14 days of request. Buyer has 3 days after receipt to void contract.
